'''Marcelo "Marcelinho" Tieppo Huertas''' (born 25 May 1983) is a Brazilian professional [[basketball]] player and the [[captain (sports)|team captain]] for [[CB Canarias]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]]. He has represented the [[Brazil national basketball team|Brazilian national basketball team]] in international competitions and also holds Italian citizenship.

At 32 years old, Huertas was the second oldest rookie in NBA history after [[Pablo Prigioni]] and before [[Andre Ingram]]. After signing with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2015, he played one and a half seasons before returning to Spain in 2017. In [[2024-25 ACB season|2025]], Huertas won the [[ACB Most Valuable Player|Liga ACB MVP]] award at 42 years of age.<ref name=mvp>{{cite news |title=¡Marcelinho Huertas, MVP Movistar de la Liga Endesa 2024-25! |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/511787-marcelinho-huertas-mvp-movistar-de-la-liga-endesa-202425.html |access-date=27 May 2025 |work=www.acb.com |date=27 May 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Early years in Brazil and Texas===
Huertas began his career playing with the youth basketball teams of the [[sports club|multi-sports club]] [[Esporte Clube Pinheiros|E.C. Pinheiros]] in Brazil. After playing high school basketball at [[Coppell High School]] in [[Coppell, Texas]], he made his senior men's team debut in the 2001–02 season, with the senior men's team of [[FMU São Paulo (basketball)|FMU São Paulo]]. He then moved to [[Esporte Clube Pinheiros (basketball)|the senior men's basketball team of E.C. Pinheiros]], for the 2002–03 season, where he played in the top [[Campeonato Brasileiro de Basquete|Brazilian League]]. He then returned to FMU São Paulo for the 2003–04 season.

===Europe===
Huertas joined the [[Liga ACB]] club [[Joventut Badalona|DKV Joventut]] in 2004, playing for the [[Badalona]]-based team for three seasons until 2007. On October 2, 2004, Huertas made his debut with the Catalans in a game against [[CE Lleida Bàsquet|Lleida Bàsquet]], scoring 9 points and recording 3 assists.<ref>{{cite web |first=Ramon |last=Aymerich Villacampa |title=El curioso caso de Marcelinho Huertas | url=https://www.tiempodebasket.com/el-curioso-caso-de-marcelinho-huertas/ |website=tiempodebasquet.com |date=2 July 2024 |access-date=28 May 2025 |language=es}}</ref> With Joventut, Huertas reached the [[Liga ACB]] Playoffs for three consecutive seasons, won the [[2005-06 FIBA EuroCup]] and played in the [[2006–07 Euroleague]].<ref>{{cite web |title=El DKV Joventut se hace con el fichaje de Marcelinho Huertas | url=https://www.europapress.es/deportes/baloncesto-00163/noticia-dkv-joventut-hace-fichaje-marcelinho-huertas-20080709221109.html |website=europapress.es |date=10 July 2008 |access-date=28 May 2025 |language=es}}</ref> Still in contract with Joventut, Huertas was loaned to [[Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]] for the [[2007–08 ACB season|2007-08 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Marcelinho Huertas jugará cedido en el iurbentia Bilbao Basket esta temporada
 |url=https://www.elcorreo.com/vizcaya/20070731/deportes/bilbao-basket/marcelinho-huertas-jugara-cedido-200707311806.html |website=elcorreo.com |date=31 July 2007 |access-date=28 May 2025 |language=es}}</ref> With Bilbao, Huertas received his first [[All-Liga ACB Team]] mention.<ref>{{cite web |title=Todos los Quinteto Ideal de la temporada |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/89248 |website=acb.com |date=19 November 2012 |access-date=28 May 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

After rumors of a return to Joventut or a contract extension with Bilbao, Huertas finally signed with [[Fortitudo Pallacanestro Bologna|Fortitudo Bologna]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]], playing for the Italians during the [[2008–09 Lega Basket Serie A|2008–09 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Huertas se decide por el Fortitudo Bolonia pese al acuerdo de Bilbao con el Joventut |url=https://www.elcorreo.com/vizcaya/20080725/deportes/mas-baloncesto/huertas-decide-fortitudo-bolonia-20080725.html?ref=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.elcorreo.com%2Fvizcaya%2F20080725%2Fdeportes%2Fmas-baloncesto%2Fhuertas-decide-fortitudo-bolonia-20080725.html |website=elcorreo.com |date=25 July 2008 |access-date=28 May 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

In August 2009, Huertas signed a three-year contract with the [[Liga ACB]] club [[Saski Baskonia]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Marcelinho Huertas profile | url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Marcelinho-Huertas/Spain/Kirolbet-Baskonia-Vitoria/45804?AmNotSure=1 | publisher=EuroBasket | access-date=7 October 2018 }}</ref> He played for two seasons with the Basque team, winning the [[2009–10 ACB season|2009-10 Liga ACB]] and reaching the [[EuroLeague]] quarterfinals in both seasons.<ref>{{cite web |title=El Caja Laboral consuma la sorpresa y conquista la Liga ACB |url=https://www.libertaddigital.com/deportes/el-caja-laboral-gana-por-tercera-vez-la-liga-acb-1276395281/ |website=libertaddigital.com |date=15 June 2010 |access-date=28 May 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

====FC Barcelona (2011-2015)====
On 9 August 2011, he signed a four-year contract with [[Liga ACB]] and [[EuroLeague]] club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite news|title=FC Barcelona Official Site|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/web/catala/noticies/basquet/temporada11-12/08/09/n110809118710.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110815224446/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/web/catala/noticies/basquet/temporada11-12/08/09/n110809118710.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=15 August 2011|access-date=9 August 2011|date=9 August 2011}}</ref> Barcelona paid Baskonia 500,000 euros for the transfer.<ref>[https://www.baskonistas.com/de-ramn-rivas-a-tibor-pleiss-cronologa-de-los-traspasos-del-baskonia-al-fc-barcelona/?srsltid=AfmBOorrvP7aewsQ--gLED4d2zncmHPSX_TQQjCx6Yo721tMS5rKvtlM De Ramón Rivas a Adam Hanga, cronología de los traspasos entre el Baskonia y el FC Barcelona - baskonistas.com]</ref> With Barcelona, Huertas won the [[Liga ACB]] twice ([[2011-12 ACB season|2012]] and [[2013-14 ACB season|2014]]) and won the [[2013 Copa del Rey de Baloncesto|2013 Spanish Cup]]. He also helped the Catalans reach the [[EuroLeague Final Four]] for three consecutive years.[[File:Real Madrid-FC Barcelona mayo 2013CropedmarcelinhoP1070766.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Huertas playing for [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]] in 2013]]

Huertas became a key player in the team's rotation in his first season, leading the team in assists throughout the [[2011-12 ACB season|2011-12 season]] and helping win the [[2011 Supercopa de España de Baloncesto|Spanish Supercup]]. In the first game of the [[2012 ACB Playoffs#Finals|2012 ACB Finals]], Huertas scored a three-point [[buzzer beater]] from half-court to seal the first win in a series in which the Catalans would take the title against [[El Clásico (basketball)|rivals]] [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref name=acb>{{cite news|title=Marcelinho Huertas pone fin a su trayectoria en el FC Barcelona|url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/115208|website=acb.com|access-date=28 May 2025|date=12 August 2015}}</ref>

Huertas would again be instrumental in the [[2013-14 ACB season|2013-14 Liga ACB]] win, playing 40 minutes and scoring the game-winning shot in a key [[2014 ACB Playoffs#Semifinals|semifinal]] game against [[Valencia Basket]].<ref name=acb />

===Los Angeles Lakers (2015–2017)===
On 9 September 2015, Huertas signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/150909_huertasSigns|title=Lakers Sign Marcelo Huertas|work=NBA.com|date=9 September 2015|access-date=9 September 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Lakers in the team's season opener against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] on 28 October, recording 2 points, 2 rebounds, and 2 assists in a 112–111 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Wolves edge Lakers 112-111 in first game since Flip's death|work=NBA.com|date=28 October 2015|access-date=29 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151026213514/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=26 October 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 6 March 2016, he recorded season-highs of 10 points and 9 assists in a 112–95 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160306/GSWLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Lakers stun Warriors 112-95 for Golden State's 6th loss|work=NBA.com|date=6 March 2016|access-date=12 March 2016}}</ref> Four days later, he had a season-best game with 13 points and 5 assists in a 120–108 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160310/CLELAL/gameinfo.html|title=In LeBron's final duel with Kobe, Cavs top Lakers 120-108|work=NBA.com|date=10 March 2016|access-date=11 March 2016}}</ref>

On 5 August 2016, Huertas re-signed with the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/160805huertas|title=Lakers Sign Marcelo Huertas|work=NBA.com|date=5 August 2016|access-date=5 August 2016}}</ref> On 23 February 2017, Huertas was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Tyler Ennis (basketball)|Tyler Ennis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-compete-two-trades|title=Rockets Compete Two Trades|work=NBA.com|date=23 February 2017|access-date=23 February 2017}}</ref> Upon being acquired by the Rockets, Huertas was waived by the team.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=HoustonRockets|number=835652493119995904|date=25 February 2017|title=Roster Update: Rockets GM Daryl Morey announced today that the team has waived guard Marcelo Huertas.}}</ref>

===Return to Spain===
==== Baskonia (2017–2019) ====
On 25 July 2017, Huertas signed a two-year deal with [[Saski Baskonia]], returning to the team he left in 2011.<ref>{{cite news|title=Baskonia, Huertas reunite after six seasons apart|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7ydyykunns6mulnt|access-date=25 July 2017|work=EuroLeague.net|date=25 July 2017|language=en}}</ref> In the [[2017-18 ACB season|2017-18 season]] Huertas reached the [[2018 ACB Playoffs#Finals|Liga ACB Finals]], which Baskonia would ultimately lose to [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news|title=El Real Madrid recupera el título de la ACB con Rudy Fernández 'MVP'
|url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/deportes/baloncesto/acb/2018-06-19/real-madrid-campeon-liga-baskonia-rudy-fernandez_1581339/|access-date=28 May 2025|work=elconfidencial.com|date=19 June 2018|language=es}}</ref> During both seasons with Baskonia, Huertas reached the [[EuroLeague]] playoffs.[[File:Marcelo Huertas 9 - Saski Baskonia 20171215.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Huertas with [[Baskonia]] in 2017]]

Huertas' second stint at Baskonia ended in June 2019 having played 142 games over two seasons and averaging 7.8 [[points per game]] and 5 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] during the second season. During his two spells with the [[Vitoria-Gasteiz]]-based team, he played 260 official games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Marcelinho Huertas cierra su segunda etapa como baskonista|url=https://www.baskonia.com/marcelinho-huertas-cierra-su-segunda-etapa-como-baskonista/|access-date=28 May 2025|work=baskonia.com|date=11 June 2019|language=es}}</ref>

==== Canarias (2019–present) ====
On 23 July 2019, Huertas signed a two-year deal with [[CB 1939 Canarias|CB Canarias]] (known as Iberostar Tenerife for sponsorship reasons).<ref>{{cite news |title=ACB.COM - Experiencia para el timón de Iberostar Tenerife: ¡Llega Marcelinho Huertas! |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=147358 |access-date=23 July 2019 |work=acb.com |date=23 July 2019 |language=es-ES |archive-date=23 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723220932/http://acb.com/redaccion.php?id=147358 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He averaged 12.9 points and 8.3 assists per game in his debut season for Canarias. Huertas re-signed with the team on 4 June 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Iberostar Tenerife extend Marcelinho Huertas |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/iberostar-tenerife-extend-marcelinho-huertas/ |website=Sportando |access-date=4 June 2020 |date=4 June 2020}}</ref>

Huertas became a star player for the team, and he was named to the [[BCL Star Lineup|All-Basketball Champions League First Team]] in 2020, before winning the [[2021-22 Basketball Champions League]] and being named [[Basketball Champions League Final Four MVP|Final Four MVP]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.championsleague.basketball/19-20/news/star-lineup-revealed-alocen-best-young-player|title=Star Lineup revealed, Alocen Best Young Player|date=29 September 2020|access-date=8 October 2020|work=[[Basketball Champions League]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gigantes.com/bcl/marcelinho-huertas-se-lleva-el-mvp-de-la-final-four-de-la-basketball-champions-league/|title=Marcelinho Huertas se lleva el MVP de la Final Four de la Basketball Champions League |date=8 May 2022|access-date=28 May 2025|website=gigantes.com|language=es}}</ref> Continuing to play a key role in Tenerife's performances in the [[Basketball Champions League]] every web|url=https://www.championsleague.basketball/23-24/news/mvp-huertas-coach-spanoulis-headline-bcl-season-8-award-winners|title=MVP Huertas, coach Spanoulis headline BCL Season 8 award winners|date=27 2025|access-date=28 May 2025|work=[[Basketball Champions League]]}}</ref> He also won the [[2020 FIBA Intercontinental Cup|2020]] and [[2023 FIBA Intercontinental Cup|2023]] [[FIBA Intercontinental |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=10 February 2020 |title=MVP Huertas hails Tenerife's team spirit, coaching staff |publisher=[[FIBA|FIBA.com]] |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/intercontinentalcup/2020/news/mvp-huertas-hails-tenerife-s-team-spirit-coaching-staff |access-date=21 November 2020}}</ref>

In his 18th season in the [[Liga ACB]], the [[2024-25 ACB season|2024-25 season]], Huertas won the [[ACB Most Valuable Player]] award, in addition to being named to the [[All-Liga ACB Team|All-Liga ACB First Team]] for the fifth time. Huertas had turned 42 just prior to earning the award.<ref name=mvp />

==National team career==
Huertas has been a member of the senior men's [[Brazil national basketball team|Brazilian national basketball team]]. With Brazil's senior national team, he won the gold medal at the [[2005 FIBA Americas Championship]], the 2006 [[South American Basketball Championship|South American Championship]], the [[Basketball at the 2007 Pan American Games|2007 Pan American Games]], and the [[2009 FIBA Americas Championship]]. He also won the silver medal at the [[2011 FIBA Americas Championship]].

He also played at the following tournaments: the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]], the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]], the [[2013 FIBA Americas Championship]], the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]],  the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]], the [[2019 FIBA World Championship]], the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], and the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics - Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]].
